title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The UK government has responded to the 2020 Committee report on AI and public standards by committing to clearer rules on transparency, safety and accountability for AI systems. It plans to work with industry, academia and civil society to develop robust standards, enforce data protection and build public trust while supporting innovation.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual explains how it will oversee and regulate the use of artificial intelligence in exams and qualifications, aiming to keep tests fair, secure, and credible. The policy was issued after a request from the Secretaries of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade to provide clear guidance on AI’s role in the qualifications sector.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyrighted materials are used in training AI systems and assesses the legal and ethical implications of such use. It offers recommendations to balance protection of creators' rights with fostering innovation in AI development.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government has released a reply to the House of Lords' AI report, “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” outlining its plans to boost AI safety, support innovation, and protect workers. It stresses that AI should be developed responsibly, with clear rules, funding, and partnership between public and private sectors.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document defines the scope, purpose, and responsibilities of a committee that will review how artificial intelligence should align with and influence public standards. It also includes a set of FAQs that explain the committee’s work, process, and expected outcomes.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has supplied written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry into AI governance, presenting its perspective on policy, risk management, and ethical considerations. The submission seeks to shape the committee’s recommendations for regulating artificial intelligence development and deployment.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The document explores how artificial intelligence is reshaping the rules that govern medical products, looking at new safety standards and testing procedures. It explains how the recommendations from the AI White Paper can be put into practice to ensure AI‑driven medical devices are reliable, transparent, and protect patients.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence AI Strategy sets out the goal of becoming the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential defence organisation in artificial intelligence for a country of our size. It aims to use AI to improve defence operations, build confidence, and maintain a leading position in technology and strategy.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport industry to capture the benefits of AI while carefully addressing its risks. It provides a roadmap of strategies, collaboration mechanisms, and risk‑management steps to ensure AI is used safely and effectively across the sector.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report tracks how AI developers are using copyrighted materials in training and model creation, highlighting compliance with the Data (Use and Access) Act's Section 137. It outlines current practices, challenges, and recommendations for balancing innovation with copyright protection.
